items.q: What is the difference between a scalar and a vector?
items.correct: Vectors have direction (force, velocity); scalars don't (mass, speed).
items.random_wrong: Scalars have direction but vectors don't.
items.why: A vector needs both magnitude and direction; a scalar has magnitude only.

items.correct: No — precise is repeatable; accurate is close to the true value.
items.random_wrong: Repeating a reading removes systematic error.
items.why: You can be precise but inaccurate; repeats reduce random, not systematic, error.

items.q: Does adding more decimal places make a measurement more accurate?
items.correct: No — figures beyond the instrument's resolution don't add accuracy.
items.misconception: Yes, more decimal places always means more accuracy.
items.random_wrong: Significant figures don't matter in science.
items.why: Report figures consistent with the instrument's precision; extra digits are meaningless.
